classification.difficultyReason: Complete a supplied co-interior, straight-angle and opposite-angle reasoning chain with alternative checks.

inlines.text: If you have a choice of reasons, use them to check your answers.

spec.description: Two steep parallel lines descend rightwards and are crossed by a shallow descending transversal. Matching single parallel arrows lie above the intersections. Unknown a is upper-right at the left intersection; 50° upper-left, b lower-left and c lower-right at the right intersection. Six unlabelled endpoints, no arcs.
spec.mathematics: a and 50° are co-interior; a and b are alternate interior; c and 50° are vertically opposite. Coordinates preserve the source's schematic appearance, not measured angles.

answer.short: Blanks in order: $180$; $130$; $180$; $130$; $130$; alternate.; $50$; vertically.; straight; $50$
answer.worked:
$a+50^\circ=180^\circ$ (co-interior angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}a&=180^\circ-50^\circ\\a&=130^\circ\end{align*}$$

$b+50^\circ=180^\circ$ (straight angle).

$$\begin{align*}b&=180^\circ-50^\circ\\b&=130^\circ\end{align*}$$

$b=a=130^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines), agreeing with the straight-angle calculation.

$c=50^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).

$c+b=180^\circ$ (straight angle).

$$\begin{align*}c&=180^\circ-130^\circ\\c&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
This agrees with the vertically opposite angle.
